blocks.x: From Carrie Bradshaw’s Manolo-clad strolls toward the Central Park pond to the infamous Gossip Girl series finale, when Chuck and Blair finally said “I do,” the Bethesda Terrace Arcade has had quite the run on both the big and small screens. The spot feels incredibly familiar even if you’ve never been there yourself — thanks in no small part to the countless movies, TV shows, and love stories that have used it as a backdrop.

And let’s be real: Central Park has always been something of a rom-com character in its own right. But Bethesda Terrace, and the ornate arcade tucked beneath it, feels especially cinematic. With its sweeping staircase, fountain views, intricate tilework, and dreamy vaulted ceiling, it’s practically begging for a dramatic meet-cute, a tearful goodbye, or a very New York declaration of love.

Of course, the arcade’s history began long before Carrie’s column even began or Serena van der Woodsen first wandered through the park. Long before the Upper East Side’s most glamorous fictional residents made the area their playground, this hidden-in-plain-sight landmark was already captivating New Yorkers with its remarkable architecture and craftsmanship.
History of the Bethesda Terrace Arcade

Designed in the 1860s by Jacob Wrey Mould as part of Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux’s master plan, the Arcade was conceived as a grand covered hall connecting the park’s Mall to the lake. Its crown jewel is the ceiling: 15,876 hand-crafted encaustic tiles produced by Minton’s Ltd. in England. Divided into 49 panel patterns, it remains the only ceiling in the entire world featuring this intricate, floor-style Minton tilework.
The 2007 Restoration

Over a century of severe water infiltration and freeze-thaw cycles forced the Central Park Conservancy to remove the decaying tiles in 1983. Following decades of specialized preservation work and a monumental $7 million restoration effort, expert technicians painstakingly reinstalled all 16,000 tiles using custom steel backing plates, reopening the grand passageway to the public in 2007 in all its 19th-century glory.
Where You Can See It in Pop Culture
Gossip Girl: Chuck and Blair’s quickie wedding under the arches in the emotional series finale.
Sex and the City: A recurring backdrop for Carrie, Miranda, Charlotte, and Samantha’s heart-to-hearts.
When Harry Met Sally: Harry and Sally stroll through the arcade during their autumn walk through the park.
Enchanted: Giselle bursts into the show-stopping “That’s How You Know” musical number right along the terrace.
The Avengers: The team gathers under the arcade before Thor takes Loki and the Tesseract back to Asgard.
Home Alone 2: Lost in New York: Kevin McCallister dodges the Sticky Bandits near the arcade’s iconic staircases.

Know before you go
Location: Central Park at 72nd Street, mid-park (just south of the Bethesda Fountain and the Lake).
How to Get There: Take the 6 train to 68th St–Hunter College or 77th St, or the B or C train to 72nd St, then take a short walk toward the center of the park.

Visitor Details: Open daily from 6:00 AM to 1:00 AM with free entry; visit early in the morning to beat the crowds or drop by in the afternoon to catch acoustic street performers making full use of the vault’s rich echo.
